research_topic: How is immune homeostasis maintained and regulated?
scope: Individual human immune variation, regulation, mucosal barrier and microbiota crosstalk, immune memory, longitudinal multi-omics, and human-relevant microphysiological models.
allowed_conclusions: Immune homeostasis is an individualized, dynamic, and compartmental feedback process rather than a universal static setpoint.
Longitudinal human measurements and human-relevant platforms can test bounded hypotheses about resilience and regulation.
Any clinical interpretation or intervention requires qualified human review and independent validation.
prohibited_conclusions: A single biomarker or blood snapshot diagnoses immune homeostasis.
An animal or organ-on-chip finding proves efficacy in humans.
The proposed research has rebalanced a person's immune system or produced observed clinical results.

evidence_cards.claim: Human immune states vary substantially among individuals.
Healthy baseline immune variation and pre-vaccination predictors can be measured in humans.
Longitudinal multi-omics reveals large between-person variation with selected within-person stability.
Microbiota, immune development, containment, and regulatory responses are interconnected.
Host-microbiota interaction affects homeostasis and disease through multiple immune pathways.
Commensal microbiota contributes to immune response, colonization resistance, and inflammatory disease context.
Regulatory T cells and tolerance pathways regulate mucosal and systemic activation; preclinical transfer evidence requires translation restraint.
Human NK cell memory can be clonally maintained with stable epigenetic features.
Immunocompetent organ-on-chip models can represent selected tissue-immune interactions while retaining substantial scope limitations.
Human gut-on-chip systems can dissect selected barrier, microbial, and inflammatory contributions under controlled conditions.
Organ-on-chip systems require fit-for-purpose design and cannot be assumed to mimic all human physiology.
